To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a curriculum review process that is effective and that results in a sustainable change to the course must involve: 1) A thorough and detailed consideration of the rationale for the existence of the course; 2) The creation of a shared understanding of the aims of the course and of the underlying rationales; 3) The creation of an environment where the participants feel able to express their views and concerns; 4) An environment where the participants are able to express their own views and concerns; and

the Law Faculty should invest in a process of curriculum development that is sustainable, that is, a process that can be used in future curriculum development projects, and that can be applied across the Faculty.
